programs.name: Paid Family and Medical Leave (employee maximum)

sources.name: Massachusetts Circular M withholding tables at 5.0%, effective January 1, 2026

notes: Read from the official 2026 publication listed in sources on 2026-10-20. Not yet signed off.

Circular M percentage method: deduct FICA withheld (up to $2,000 a year) and the exemption value ($4,400 for one exemption; $3,400 plus $1,000 each for more), annualize, tax at 5% (9% above $1,107,750, the 4% surtax), head of household credit $120 a year. No withholding when wages are under $8,000 a year for employees claiming an exemption.
A claimed spouse counts as 4 exemptions on Form M-4. Blindness credits are not modelled.
Checked against the official weekly wage-bracket table (wages $300-$310 withhold $14.08 with 0 exemptions and $9.85 with 1), asserted in tests.

PFML: 0.88% total in 2026; employers may withhold up to 40% of the medical part (0.28%) and up to all of the family part (0.18%), a maximum of 0.46% from the employee, up to the Social Security wage cap. The calculator assumes the employee pays the maximum.
